USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Publish the final Section 301 list and implement the already-announced 25% duties on about $50 billion of Chinese industrial and technology goods, targeted at sectors tied to Made in China 2025. Do not expand immediately to a $100 billion list, and do not reopen the ZTE denial order now that a $1 billion fine-plus-monitors settlement exists. Keep a negotiating channel open for structural IP, licensing, and investment issues, but treat additional Chinese purchase promises as insufficient to pause the tariffs after the May 19 truce collapsed.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is a mild US opportunity, not a high-cost shock. The Section 301 record (22 Mar and 3 Apr 2018) documents forced tech transfer, JV/licensing pressure, directed acquisitions, and cyber-enabled IP theft, with interagency harm estimated at least $50 billion a year — the same scale as the proposed tariff list aimed at aerospace, ICT, robotics, and machinery. China answered with a matching $50 billion list aimed at soybeans, autos, and aircraft (4 Apr), and already levied about $3 billion after the Section 232 metals tariffs (2 Apr), so farm-belt exposure is real: China takes a majority of US soybean exports. Those retaliatory duties are still contingent on US implementation, and US macros as of mid-June show no material hit: industrial production is up, Michigan sentiment is 98.2, VIX is back near 13 after a brief 17 spike on 29 May, and goods imports from China remain ~$44 billion a month versus ~$11 billion of US exports to China. That asymmetry, plus the April ZTE denial order that effectively shut the firm, is leverage. China already offered to “significantly increase” purchases on 19 May; the White House correctly resumed 301 on 29 May after getting no structural IP concessions. Early-June Ross–Liu talks produced no breakthrough, and Beijing said purchase outcomes would be void if the US imposed tariffs. Implementing the announced $50 billion is therefore the coherent next step: it prices the documented IP harm and keeps pressure on after a failed truce, without the second-order spiral of an immediate $100 billion expansion that would lock in soybean/aircraft retaliation and raise recession and ally-cohesion risk. The 7 Jun ZTE settlement (fine, board change, embedded monitors) already extracted a costly non-tariff concession; re-killing ZTE now would collide with a bipartisan Senate NDAA push and with the just-completed Singapore diplomacy, while walking back 301 would reward stalling.
key_factors: Section 301 finding of forced tech transfer and ~$50B annual harm, still unanswered by structural Chinese concessions
May 19 purchase-only truce collapsed on May 29; early-June Ross-Liu talks failed and Beijing conditioned any deal on no US tariffs
US real economy not yet hit (IP, sentiment, VIX); bilateral trade still ~4:1 China-to-US goods flow
China's contingent $50B retaliation is concentrated on soybeans, autos, and aircraft — politically costly if the fight widens
ZTE denial order showed firm-level US leverage; 7 Jun compliance deal already cashed that chip without needing a new death sentence

sources_cited.excerpt: USTR releases Section 301 report finding China's IP/tech-transfer practices unreasonable or discriminatory. Trump signs presidential memorandum directing tariffs on Chinese imports, a WTO case, and investment restrictions.
USTR publishes proposed Section 301 tariff list: ~1,300 Chinese product lines (~$50B), targeting aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery and related sectors.
China announces proposed retaliatory tariffs on ~$50B of US goods (including soybeans, automobiles, and aircraft) in response to the Section 301 list.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold."
White House announces the US will proceed with Section 301 actions, including 25% tariffs on ~$50B of Chinese imports. Truce collapses.
US industrial production latest 103.198 (2018-06-01), up ~1.7% over the window — no visible production shock from the dispute.
Michigan consumer sentiment 98.2 in June 2018 — still elevated; no confidence collapse.
VIX 12.94 on 2018-06-13 after a 17.02 spike on 2018-05-29 when the truce collapsed; markets not pricing crisis.
US goods imports from China still $44.5B in June vs EXPCH $10.9B — large bilateral imbalance remains US leverage.
Interagency estimate that China's tech-transfer policies harm the US economy by at least $50 billion per year; 25% duties proposed commensurate with that harm.
As of 12 Jun 2018, administration expected to publish the final $50B list as soon as Friday; Ross-Liu talks failed to clinch purchase deals; China warned outcomes void if US raised tariffs.
China: all economic and trade outcomes of the talks will not take effect if the US imposes any trade sanctions, including raising tariffs. US soybean exports to China >$12B.
7 Jun deal: ZTE pays $1B, replaces board/leadership, accepts US-picked compliance monitors; US to lift seven-year denial order.
Bipartisan Senate NDAA amendment (Cotton/Van Hollen/Schumer) seeks to restore ZTE penalties and bar US government purchases from ZTE and Huawei.
China purchases 61% of total US soybean exports and more than 30% of overall US soybean production; farm groups warned a 25% Chinese tariff would be devastating.
